I have a lot of trouble making the NVidia driver work with my "dual monitor" setup, largely because it consists of an external monitor positioned to the left of my laptop, the native screen of which I use as my secondary. Apparently, the standard setup is reversed, so I have had to fight tooth and nail to get my monitors to behave in the past, using both the native display tools of whatever desktop environment I was using at the time, and the nvidia-settings. But nothing really sticks, and it's something I have to go through every time I log in.

Thankfully, somebody smarter than me figured out how to make xrandr do everything I needed it to, and I wrote a little script that I can fire off on login. There's not a whole lot of specifics I can impart to you because I don't know your setup. But go Google xrandr and see if you can address your problems via the command line -- you can set your resolution, desktop position, and primary screen, all with one line of code. Then it's just a matter of sticking that in your startup somewhere, and you're golden.
